A.explanation: Starts at maximum positive $X$ at $t=0$, a shift of about $125\,\mu\text{s}$ or $T/4$. A distance of one wavelength does not give a quarter-period shift.

B.explanation: Starts at $0$ going negative, the opposite motion to the original. This is a half-period or antiphase shift, not a whole-wavelength shift.

C.explanation: Starts negative and crosses upward at $125\,\mu\text{s}$. This is about a quarter-period delay, not the one-period delay for $0.165\,\text{m}$.

D.explanation: Identical to the original graph with $X=0$ and moving positive at $t=0$. A separation of one wavelength gives a one-period time delay, so the motion repeats.

hints: Notice the zero crossings of the given $X$-time graph at $0$, $250\,\mu\text{s}$ and $500\,\mu\text{s}$ to find the time period $T$ in $\mu\text{s}$.
Connect wave speed $v = 330\,\text{m s}^{-1}$ to wavelength using $\lambda = vT$ and compare $\lambda$ with the extra distance $0.165\,\text{m}$.
Think what time delay $\Delta t = \text{distance}/v$ means for the second molecule, and what a delay of exactly one $T$ does to a sine graph with the same zero time.
walkthrough: Read the period from the top graph. It starts at $X=0$ going positive, crosses down through zero at $250\,\mu\text{s}$ and returns to zero going positive at $500\,\mu\text{s}$, so $T = 500\,\mu\text{s} = 5.0 \times 10^{-4}\,\text{s}$.
Use $v = f\lambda = \lambda/T$ to find the wavelength: $\lambda = vT = 330 \times 5.0 \times 10^{-4} = 0.165\,\text{m}$.
The second molecule is $0.165\,\text{m}$ further away, which is exactly $1\lambda$. The wave therefore takes one extra period to reach it: $\Delta t = 0.165/330 = 5.0 \times 10^{-4}\,\text{s} = T$.

A delay of one whole period leaves a sinusoidal oscillation unchanged in phase. At the common $t=0$ the second molecule must show the same earlier part of the motion as the first molecule did one period before.
That means $X=0$ and moving positive at $t=0$, with the same $500\,\mu\text{s}$ period and zero crossings at $250\,\mu\text{s}$, $500\,\mu\text{s}$ and $750\,\mu\text{s}$. This is option D.
